title: Prefill/Decode sampling window and kernel concurrency profiling
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Add a lightweight, production-safe profiling harness that samples fixed-duration execution windows across prefill and decode phases to capture per-kernel concurrency patterns, queueing, and latency contribution. The goal is to produce per-model heatmaps and request-level attributions that help tune the kernel selector (heuristics for attention path, fused vs separated kernels) and scheduling thresholds without adding meaningful overhead to steady-state serving.
background: Current NVTX-based tracing surfaces high-level spans but doesn't provide consistent sampling across short-lived kernels or capture transient concurrency spikes that occur when prefill and decode overlap. This makes it hard to tune the kernel selector and prefill/decode scheduler for tail latency. We need probes that correlate kernel launches, GPU queue depth, and approximate SM occupancy to explain regressions and recommend selection changes.
proposed_approach: Implement a periodic sampling thread in the runtime that opens fixed "execution windows" (configurable 50-200ms) and collects per-stream kernel names, launch timestamps, and simple occupancy estimates via existing runtime counters (cupti/perf or lightweight CUDA queries).

Emit a compressed 'window summary' event (no raw token traces) with: top-3 kernels by cumulative time, max concurrent kernels, median kernel latency, and a coarse occupancy bucket (0-25%,25-50%,50-75%,75-100%).

Correlate window summaries with the existing trace spans by attaching the window_id to NVTX ranges and the request span when available, enabling aggregation into heatmaps along dimensions: model, route, batch-size, phase (prefill/decode), and kernel-type.

Add a runtime flag to enable low-overhead mode that samples 1% of windows and a debug mode that samples 100% for short runs. Ensure sampling adds <1% CPU and <2% p95 token latency overhead in low-overhead mode.

Surface results in Console: a new 'Kernel Concurrency' tile with time-series of max concurrent kernels, heatmap view, and automated recommendations for kernel-selector thresholds (e.g., prefer fused-attn when concurrency>4 and seq_len>X).
acceptance_criteria: Runtime emits window_summary events with schema matching analytics contract (fields: window_id, start_ts, duration_ms, top_kernels, max_concurrency, occupancy_bucket, phase_hint, model, route, batch_size).
Console shows a Kernel Concurrency tile for internal testing clusters and a heatmap for at least two models (gpt-small and gpt-medium) with prefill/decode split.
Low-overhead sampling measured: <1% CPU increase and <=2% p95 token latency increase on standard benchmark harness at 95th percentile. Debug sampling documented and gated behind config.
Kernel selector tuning documented with at least one automated recommendation that, when applied in A/B, reduces median cost-per-token for a test workload by >=6% without regressing output quality.
notes: We intentionally avoid streaming raw per-token kernel traces; window summaries are compressed to control volume. Implementation will reuse existing NVTX attach points to map windows to request spans. If CUPTI counters are not available in a given deployment, we will fall back to kernel name + queue-depth heuristics.
comments: 2026-02-18 Ava Martinez: Triage - collated user reports and internal p95 regressions that indicate transient concurrency spikes during mixed prefill/decode workloads. Filing this ticket to prototype window-sampling approach.

2026-02-22 Ravi Shah: Initial design draft posted to Confluence. Plan to prototype in canary runtime with 50ms default window and 1% sampling. Need to confirm CUPTI availability across Dedicated clusters.

2026-02-27 Morgan Li: Reviewed approach; suggested adding occupancy buckets to avoid raw counter storage and to make Console visualizations actionable. Also requested a perf gate for low-overhead mode.

2026-03-03 Elena Petrova: Implemented PoC in runtime branch. PoC emits window_summary to local event sink and renders heatmaps offline. Observed concurrency spikes correlated with specific attention kernel variants.
2026-03-09 Ravi Shah: Ran benchmark on canary with low-overhead sampling. Overhead measured at ~0.8% CPU and p95 latency increase 1.6% on gpt-medium with batch-size 8. Pushing PR for review.
2026-03-10 PR review feedback: address schema field naming (use occupancy_bucket instead of occ_bucket), add unit tests for sampling clock jitter, and include feature flagging at route level.
